# Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem statement

When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent work item, its descendants are left in whatever terminal or non-terminal state they previously held. This lets a parent reach `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit while its children remain `open`/`blocked`/`in_progress` (or already `done`), so downstream steps can neither treat the subtree as consistent nor close the parent without a manual `wl close --force` sweep.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer.** As a producer, when I audit a parent work item and the audit passes, I want every descendant to be marked `completed`/`done` automatically so that I never have to force-close the parent and sweep unfinished children as a side effect.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`).** As the post-release close step, I want an audit-approved parent's descendants to already be terminal so the collateral-descendant guard does not falsely refuse to close released items.
- **Secondary user — audit operators/agents.** As an audit operator, I want the cascade to be idempotent and authorised only by a passing parent audit, so reruns and failed audits never resurrect or mutate work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cascade on passing parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, i.e. `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` on the success path), every descendant is set to `status=completed, stage=done`, and each cascaded child receives an explanatory comment naming the authorising parent and the audit timestamp.
- [ ] **AC2 — Idempotent and `deleted`-safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree produces no further mutations or duplicate comments; `deleted` descendants are skipped; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cascade without a passing audit.** A parent audit that fails (`Ready to close: No`), is fallback-tainted, or has not been run performs **no** cascade and leaves descendants untouched. Cascading is authorised by a passing audit verdict only — never by status/stage alone.
- [ ] **AC4 — Ship close step closes the parent without a refusal.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (`done`/`deleted`) without a refusal, covered by unit tests that inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests cover the behaviour.** Passing-parent → children done (with comments); failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only the appropriate action; cascade rerun → no further mutation (testing/validation criterion).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing audit and ship suites pass.** The existing audit runner and ship suites pass and `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` as applicable).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The cascade must live where the verdict is known — the parent audit success path in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
- Any `wl` mutations must respect the `StatusLifecycle` claim invariant (an item must be `in_progress` before mutation) and route `--worklog-dir` through the shared resolution helpers so the cascade targets the item's own worklog store regardless of cwd.
- The cascade must not weaken the existing scope guard (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H): a parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants.
- Must remain safe under dry-run (`--do-not-persist`): a dry-run passing verdict must not mutate descendants.

## Existing state

- **Verdict knowledge.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` computes the parent verdict at `audit_verdict = _parse_ready_to_close(report)` (~line 11363) and, in the terminal transition block, takes the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch (~line 11773) to run `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (or `--stage done` when already done). This is the natural single point to trigger the cascade.
- **Child-state checks today.** `_check_children_stages` / related helpers already classify children in `in_review`/`done` as exempt but do **not** mutate them; `inherited_pass` records a verdict reuse but never sets `completed`/`done`.
- **Ship close step.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (~line 370) computes `candidateIds` from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only) and refuses a `--force` close when `collateral = descendants.filter(id => !candidateIds.has(id))` is non-empty (~line 534). Descendants already `stage=done` therefore always appear as collateral — tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.
- **Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02).** Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release, all audit-approved; the close step refused all five (25 open/blocked children on two of them), and all five had to be closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done`.

## Desired change

1. Add a cascade helper (e.g. `_cascade_descendants_terminal`) in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` that, given a parent id and audit timestamp, walks descendants (`wl show <id> --children` recursively or the existing tree helpers), skips `deleted` and already `completed`/`done` items, and for each remaining descendant issues `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, followed by `wl comment add <child>` with a reason naming the parent and audit timestamp.
2. Invoke the helper from the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success branch only (and not on the failure/fallback restore branches), after the parent's own verified transition succeeds; suppress it under dry-run.
3. Make the helper idempotent (no mutation/comment when a child is already terminal) and non-fatal (a cascade failure for one child is logged and does not abort the audit, matching the ship step's non-blocking semantics).
4. Keep `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral logic unchanged apart from SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP's `done`/`deleted` exclusion (defence-in-depth).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Add the cascade helper and call it on the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success path; reuse existing descendant/`_run_wl` helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Ensure `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` excludes terminal (`done`/`deleted`) descendants from `collateral` (SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP); add/verify injected-fn unit coverage for AC4.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — New cascade regression tests (passing parent, failing parent, mixed child states, idempotent rerun, dry-run).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — Extend lifecycle-transition tests to assert cascade/no-cascade per verdict.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — Unit tests for the terminal-descendant non-refusal (AC4).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` — Document cascade-on-audit behaviour (AC7).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (in-progress) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims all children in `in_review`/`done`": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents the "unfinished children under a done parent" failure mode.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed) — "Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met".
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed) — "Audit: parent-first child pass-through".
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed) — the scope guard that must not regress.
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** (completed) — "Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits" (automated find-related match).
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** (completed) — "Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable" (automated find-related match).
- **Provenance:** filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep into the ship step.** The root fix is audit-side; touching `run-release.js` beyond the terminal-descendant exclusion risks duplicating SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP. Mitigation: keep the ship change minimal and additive.
- **Risk — partial cascade on `wl` failure.** A mid-cascade `wl` failure could leave a subtree half-terminal. Mitigation: per-child try/except, loud logging, idempotent rerun, non-fatal semantics; the next audit success completes the cascade.
- **Risk — comment noise / non-idempotence.** Re-auditing a passing parent must not duplicate comments. Mitigation: skip already-terminal children before commenting; test the rerun path (AC2/AC5).
- **Risk — regression to the audit scope guard.** Cascading on a *failed* verdict would bypass SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H. Mitigation: cascade only on the `audit_verdict == "yes"` branch; explicit failing-parent test (AC3/AC5).
- **Assumption.** "Descendants" means the full recursive subtree of the audited parent (children, grandchildren, …), consistent with `wl close --force`'s recursive sweep.
- **Assumption.** A passing parent audit is the sole authorisation signal; `status`/`stage` alone never authorises a cascade.
- **Assumption.** `deleted` descendants are historical and must never be re-marked or commented on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Are any clarifications required beyond the seed context? — **Answer (producer, via the filed work item SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP and the TCE v0.1.19 release retro, 2026-10-02):** No. The seed context specifies the policy, the concrete requested fix ("when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `completed`/`done`"), the desired behaviour (5 points), the acceptance criteria, and the related work. The interview was therefore skipped per the intake "seed context suffices" rule.
- **Q:** Where should the cascade live? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §2):** In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` on the parent audit success path — a single source of truth where the verdict is known — not only as a special case in the ship close step. Evidence: repository inspection confirms the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` branch (~`audit_runner.py:11773`) is the success transition point.
- **Q:** How should `deleted` and already-terminal descendants be treated? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §3):** `deleted` children are left untouched; reruns are no-ops; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
data.title: Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

# Add the project CTA to the Discord release report

**Work item:** SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K · **Type:** bug · **Priority:** critical · **Stage:** intake_complete

## Problem statement

Projects can define a call-to-action (CTA) in their worklog config
(`.worklog/config.yaml` → `cta: "…"`), but the ship skill's post-release
Discord report never reads or renders it. A release announcement is therefore
posted **without** the project's CTA, even though it is already defined.

Concrete example — `AI_Hell/.worklog/config.yaml`:

```yaml
cta: "[Play the alpha release](https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/). Provide feedback in [Discord](https://discord.gg/gUKQTFkzQ4)"
```

This CTA was added by `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS` (AI_Hell commit `317dd70c`), but
release announcements still omit it.

## Users and user stories

**User story (release manager / producer):** As the person cutting a release,
when the ship skill posts the announcement to Discord, I want the project's
configured CTA included so the audience can immediately act on it (play the
alpha, join Discord, etc.).

**User story (project maintainer):** As a maintainer, when I set `cta:` in
`.worklog/config.yaml`, I expect it to appear automatically in every release
announcement without bespoke per-project changes.

## Root cause (verified in source)

`skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` resolves `discord.webhook_url`,
`projectName` and `projectDescription` from the three-layer worklog config
(private → project → global), but there is **no** `readCtaFromConfig` /
`resolveCta` and `buildDiscordPayload()` has no `cta` parameter. Paragraph
composition (composition AC5) is currently:

`pitch` → `focus` → `**<projectName> v<version>**` → `changelog`

so the configured `cta` is never emitted. (Confirmed: `grep -ri cta skill/ship`
returns no CTA handling.)

## Desired change

Read the `cta` key from the worklog config with the **same precedence** as the
existing keys and include it as its own paragraph in the release embed,
**after the intro block and before the changelog**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Config resolution.** `discord-notify.js` exposes `readCtaFromConfig(configPath)` and `resolveCta(projectRoot, options)`; the key `cta` is read with the same three-layer precedence (private → project → global) as `discord.webhook_url`, `projectName` and `projectDescription`. Markdown link syntax in the value is preserved verbatim.
- **AC2 — Embed composition.** When a CTA is configured, `buildDiscordPayload()` includes it as a distinct paragraph placed after the intro pitch/focus/project-version block and immediately before the changelog body. When absent, the paragraph is omitted and the embed is unchanged.
- **AC3 — Non-blocking.** A missing, empty or malformed/unreadable config (or CTA) must never fail the release: the notification still sends and the CTA paragraph is simply omitted (preserves notification AC2/AC3).
- **AC4 — Truncation preserved.** The composed embed description, including the CTA, is truncated to the Discord 4096-char limit with the ellipsis marker (preserves notification AC4).
- **AC5 — Tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) CTA present and correct ordering relative to pitch/focus/changelog; (b) CTA absent → omitted; (c) three-layer precedence; (d) malformed/unreadable config → omitted, non-blocking. A test asserts the AI_Hell-style CTA string is present in the composed payload.
- **AC6 — End-to-end example.** Given `AI_Hell/.worklog/config.yaml`, a simulated release notification for that project contains `[Play the alpha release](https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/)…` in the embed description.
- **AC7 — Docs.** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and the relevant `skill/ship/docs/` page document the `cta` config key, its precedence, and its placement in the Discord report; code comments updated.
- **AC8 — Test suite.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Notification failures must remain non-blocking (release exit code unchanged).
- Keep the existing minimal `parseSimpleYaml` subset parser; no new runtime dependencies.
- Preserve the existing Discord embed description cap (4096 chars) and the existing paragraph ordering for pitch/focus/version/changelog (composition AC5) — the CTA is additive.

## Existing state

- `cta` is a supported worklog config key (Context Hub); `AI_Hell/.worklog/config.yaml` defines one.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` supports `projectDescription` (pitch), `projectName` and `release focus`, but not `cta`.
- Existing tests: `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-discord-notify.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — add `readCtaFromConfig`/`resolveCta`, thread `cta` through `buildDiscordPayload` and `sendReleaseNotification`, add the CTA paragraph.
- `tests/unit/test-discord-notify.mjs` — unit tests for resolution + composition + non-blocking.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — extend suite coverage.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/*` — document the `cta` key and placement.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` — end-to-end wiring assertion if applicable.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K** — this item (pre-existing; upgraded to critical/bug).
- **SA-0MUVWL09T001N5P4** — Discord embed composition: pitch, focus, ordering (completed) — defines composition AC5 ordering the CTA must slot into.
- **SA-0MUU45U8Q008MKGK** — Discord release report: project elevator pitch and per-release focus paragraphs (completed).
- **SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z** — Ship skill: send Discord message with release details (completed) — origin of the embed.
- **WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS** — added the project CTA to `AI_Hell/.worklog/config.yaml` (AI_Hell commit `317dd70c`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "CTA" means the worklog `cta` config key, and "the Discord report" means the ship skill's post-release notification (`discord-notify.js`). Confirmed by the operator.
- **Risk (low):** Embed 4096-char limit may truncate the changelog when the CTA is long — mitigated by the existing truncation and AC4.
- **Scope creep:** do not add CTA rendering to other notification surfaces (e.g. standups) in this item; create linked items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (intake):** Which config should hold the CTA, and what change is wanted? **Answer (operator, interactive):** "If it is already defined then it is not being used in generating the discord report when a release is cut. Create a critical work item in ../SorraAgents." Evidence: `.worklog/config.yaml` (AI_Hell) defines `cta`; `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` has no CTA handling.
- **Q (intake):** Should the CTA drop or keep the Discord-feedback sentence? **Answer:** N/A — the task is to render whatever the project configured; the config value is unchanged.

**HEADLINE (operator guidance):** This project is game-development focused — a human is expected to be present throughout development, and the workflow assumes human creativity is central. Most skills are not game-specific, but the process is not intended to run fully autonomously on non-game infrastructure decisions.

## Findings while implementing this child (SA-0MTLJUK60000RTK1)

**Parent state.** SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM is already implemented and audited
(commit 9433e598 on dev; audit "Ready to close: Yes"), yet it sits at
status `in-progress` / stage `plan_complete` and now has this audit-created
open child.

**Scope reality.** The child is scoped as "add integration tests", but
satisfying its ACs (real-`wl` tree iteration and coverage mutation) exposed
latent defects in `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`:

1. `order_by_dependencies()` fetches dependency edges from the **parent**, not
   the children, and does not parse the real `wl dep list` JSON shape
   (`{"item":..., "inbound":[...], "outbound":[...]}`). Real child-to-child
   dependency ordering is therefore never applied.
2. `run_coverage_review()` can never return `recommendation: "auto_close"`:
   `compute_coverage()` treats a match at >= 0.4 as covered while
   `resolve_coverage_gaps()` only "resolves" at >= 0.85, so an uncovered AC can
   never be resolved. The auto-close path is dead code.
3. There is no production function to *apply* a coverage review (create/update
   a child AC, write a comment, advance the stage or stop). Mutation exists
   only as agent instructions in `plan`/`intake` SKILL.md, so child AC3/AC4
   (mutation behaviour) cannot be tested end-to-end without new production code.

**Proposed scope (needs producer decision).** Fix (1) and (2) minimally in
`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py`, add an `apply_coverage_review()` helper for
(3), then add real-`wl` integration tests (ephemeral temp `.worklog` store) plus
docs. This expands the child beyond "tests only".

**Question for the producer:** proceed with the scoped production fixes plus
integration tests under this child, or split the production fixes into a
separate work item and keep this child test-only?

Blocked on producer direction before making production changes.
